players.appliedToThePlayerStanding: Applied to the player standing on the server, so they see it happen.
players.levelsAreWhatThePlayer: Levels are what the player sees over their hotbar.
players.pointsAreWhatALevel: Points are what a level is made of, and a level costs more of them the higher it is.
players.toAnotherPlayerWhoIs: To another player who is on, or to a place.
players.dragToRearrangeItOr: Drag to rearrange it, or drop an item from the palette into a slot.
players.asTheServerLastHad: As the server last had it.
players.readFromTheRunningServer: Read from the running server, so it is where they were a moment ago.
players.whatPolarisHasWatchedAnd: What Polaris has watched, and what the world itself has counted.
players.nothingInTheLogThis: Nothing in the log this far back.
players.addAnotherAddressTheyPlay: Add another address they play from, change the note, or tie them to a Polaris account. The name itself is what the server checks.
players.aPlayerIsLetIn: A player is let in when the name is on this list and they arrive from an address registered to it.
players.anyAccountWhateverItIs: Any account, whatever it is called and whether or not it has linked Minecraft. An email that is nobody yet can be invited.
players.ifTheyHaveLinkedMinecraft: If they have linked Minecraft, their name and the addresses they connect from fill themselves in.
players.thisPolarisDoesNotShow: This Polaris does not show where other people sign in from. Ask them for the address they play from.
players.whereverTheyAreSignedIn: Wherever they are signed in to Polaris
players.thatIsNotAUsername: That is not a username this edition accepts
players.thatIsNotAnAddress: That is not an address or a range
players.polarisCouldNotReadThe: Polaris could not read the address this request came from. Type it in instead.
players.leaveItEmptyToChange: Leave it empty to change only the note.
players.useTheAddressYouAre: Use the address you are on now
players.whoThisIsForWhoever: Who this is, for whoever reads the list next. Only Polaris sees it.
players.followsDescription: {player} joins from wherever {account} is signed in to Polaris.
players.linkedDescription: {player} is {account} on Polaris. Where they join from is the addresses below.
players.tiedTo: The account they make is tied to {name}.
players.inviteFailed: The email to {email} could not be sent ({reason}). Send them this link instead.
players.inviteLink: Send {email} this link. When they make their account, it is tied to {name}.
players.invited: Invited {email}. When they make their account, it is tied to {name}.
players.followsHint: They are let in only from an address where {name} is signed in to Polaris, and removed when they sign out.
players.typedGo: The addresses typed for them go.
players.linkedHint: Linked to {name} for who they are. The addresses typed here still decide where they join from.
players.noMinecraft: {name} has not linked Minecraft, so type their username.
players.notSignedIn: {account} is not signed in to Polaris anywhere, so {player} cannot join right now.

announce.checkYourInventoryForA: Check your inventory for a gift
announce.howLongItStaysOn: How long it stays on screen
announce.theGameShowsAnAction: The game shows an action bar for about three seconds, so Polaris sends it again until the time is up.
announce.polarisKeepsSendingItUntil: Polaris keeps sending it until then. You can take it down from here at any time.

announce.everybodyWhoRunsThisServer: Everybody who runs this server can load it and send it again.

announce.previewOfTheAnnouncementIn: Preview of the announcement in the game
announce.minecraftDrawsItsOwnFont: Minecraft draws its own font, so the spacing here is close rather than exact.

vars.server: The same for everybody, read when it is sent

errors.thisServerDoesNotHave: This server does not have the /data command, so it cannot report what a player is carrying. Java 1.13 or newer can.
errors.theServerDidNotAnswer: The server did not answer, and Polaris has no copy of this player's bag yet
errors.couldNotReadTheInventory: Could not read the inventory, and Polaris has no copy of this player's bag yet
errors.theServerDidNotReport: The server did not report a position - the player has to be on the server
errors.couldNotReadThePosition: Could not read the position - the player has to be on the server
errors.couldNotReadThisPlayer: Could not read this player's history
errors.typeAPolarisUsernameOr: Type a Polaris username or email address
errors.nobodyHereGoesByThat: Nobody here goes by that. Check the username or the email address.
errors.thatPlayerIsNotOn: That player is not on this server
errors.couldNotBackUpThe: Could not back up the world
errors.checkThePackAndTry: Check the pack and try again
errors.checkTheListAndTry: Check the list and try again

world.mapsThisServerHasPlayed: Maps this server has played before. Switching restarts it.
world.everythingBuiltOnThisMap: Everything built on this map goes with it, and it is not the map the server is playing on. Back it up first if you might want it.
world.leaveBlankForARandom: Leave blank for a random world
world.aNumberOrAnyWords: A number or any words. The same seed always generates the same map.
world.theWholeOverworldIsThis: The whole overworld is this one biome. The Nether and the End are unchanged.
world.inventoriesEnderChestsStatsAnd: Inventories, ender chests, stats and advancements come across. Everyone spawns fresh on the new map.
world.bedrockKeepsPlayerDataInside: Bedrock keeps player data inside the world itself, so a new map always starts everyone over.
world.theServerRestartsToGenerate: The server restarts to generate it, so anybody playing is disconnected. The map it is on now is kept and you can switch back to it.
world.aCopyOfTheWorld: A copy of the world kept on the server's own disk, taken with saving paused so it is not caught mid-write. That covers a mistake, not a dead disk - download the ones that matter.
world.theArchiveGoesTheWorld: The archive goes; the world it was taken from is not touched.
world.copiesAreTakenOnlyWhen: Copies are taken only when you press the button.
world.noLimitOnHowMany: No limit on how many are kept.
world.takenAfterTheServerSaves: Taken after the server saves and before the container goes down, so the copy holds the last thing that happened rather than the last scheduled one.
world.aNotificationWhenAScheduled: A notification when a scheduled copy could not be taken. A server that is simply stopped is skipped quietly.
world.restoreBody: {name} restarts onto the world in this backup, so anybody playing is disconnected. The map it is on now is kept as it is - if this was the wrong backup, switch back to it under World.
world.olderGo: Older ones go once there are more than {count}.
world.budgetHint: Nought is no limit. The oldest go as the total approaches it. The newest copy is never deleted.
world.budgetHintUsed: Nought is no limit. The oldest go as the total approaches it - they take up {size} now. The newest copy is never deleted.

schedule.hoursTheServerIsKept: Hours the server is kept up, and hours it may stop once nobody is playing. Times are read where you say, not where the machine is. Nothing here restarts the server to take effect.
schedule.theZoneTheTimesAre: The zone the times are read in
schedule.minutesWithNobodyPlayingBefore: Minutes with nobody playing before a sleeping window stops it
schedule.usedOnlyByARule: Used only by a rule set to Sleep when empty.
schedule.whileItIsAsleepThe: While it is asleep the server list says so, and a player joining starts it. That attempt of theirs ends straight away - the server is only beginning to load - and joining again a minute later gets them in.
schedule.startThisServerWhenSomebody: Start this server when somebody tries to join it
schedule.whileThisServerIsAsleep: While this server is asleep its port is closed, so nobody can start it by joining. Turn on sharing the port under Address and a player arriving by name starts it again.
schedule.whileThisServerIsAsleep2: While this server is asleep its port is closed and nothing can see somebody trying to reach it, so it is started from here or by a window that says Keep running.
schedule.noWindowsYetSoThe: No windows yet, so the whole week follows the rule above.
schedule.thingsToDoAtA: Things to do at a time: restart it, warn everyone, take a backup, run a command.
schedule.thisIsWhatTheServer: This is what the server follows.
schedule.whatTheServerDoesIn: What the server does in this window
schedule.name: Name

modes.sleepHint: Stopped once nobody has played for a while. It gives its memory back, and somebody trying to join starts it again where that is possible.
modes.offHint: Stopped even if somebody is on.

schedule.quietHint: To have it go quiet without anybody starting it again, leave the schedule off and set <setting>Pause when nobody is playing</setting> under Settings. The server keeps its address, stops using the processor, and comes back the moment somebody joins.
